learningObjectives: Identify suitable use cases for cascading approvals versus a single approval
Compare the advantages of approvals using a reporting structure versus an authority matrix
Configure cascading approvals with an organizational hierarchy and with an authority matrix
Build conditional approval levels within a reporting hierarchy

elements.description: A cascade represents several required decisions in order. It is not an any-one broadcast or majority vote.

elements.text: Think of a checklist of required reviewers: a small request may need a short management list; a regulated contract may also need a reviewer from another department. Decide who belongs on the list before designing the workflow.

elements.description: Reporting structure uses management relationships; authority matrix uses a populated approver list.
Which people are required? In what order? Does the number of management levels vary? Does anyone sit outside the reporting line?
Configure rejection flow explicitly. Resolution and revision are different policies; neither majority override nor restart should be assumed.

elements.caption: The matrix may include parties outside the reporting hierarchy.

elements.description: At runtime the current-user context and selected Reporting Manager or Workgroup Manager source identify the reviewer. Do not assume the original creator is always the current user.
One requests the immediate manager; All uses the whole hierarchy; Custom uses When Rules to select the required depth. Depth is not a promise of arbitrary middle-tier skipping.

The linked v7 reporting-structure challenge uses Dev Studio, an Approve/Reject Step, Cascading and Reporting structure. Its When conditions select one or two levels; the walkthrough targets Platform 24.2.
An authority matrix needs a data structure of approvers. A Decision table, Data Page, Activity or Data Transform can populate it; a table is one supported approach.
The linked v7 challenge configures a Page List and an approver property, then a Decision table that appends required recipients. Evaluate all rows allows multiple matching results.
Use the matrix when required reviewers are outside the chosen management line. List ordering still matters; population rules are not a parallel voting mechanism.

examPitfalls.title: Series versus vote
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Cascading is not a simultaneous majority tally.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Identify every required reviewer and order.

examPitfalls.title: Manager source
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Reporting structure can use Reporting Manager or Workgroup Manager.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Inspect the selected source and current-user context.

examPitfalls.title: Matrix implementation
examPitfalls.trapDescription: An authority matrix is not synonymous with a Decision table.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Distinguish the list from its population rule.

examPitfalls.title: Conditional depth
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Custom selects required management depth; arbitrary skipping is not established by the example.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Test threshold boundaries and expected levels.

examPitfalls.title: Multiple table results
examPitfalls.trapDescription: One collected result can omit additional matching reviewers.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Check Evaluate all rows for the table-based design.

examPitfalls.title: Studio scope
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The linked challenges use Dev Studio; this does not establish a universal prohibition on other tools.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Follow the relevant version’s configuration instructions.

examPitfalls.title: Reject policy
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A displayed status or later reviewer does not establish an automatic override.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A purchase needs the requester’s management hierarchy to review in order. Which model fits?

options.text: Reporting structure
A parallel majority ballot
A status label only
A single approval that omits the other required managers

practiceQuiz.rationale: Reporting structure follows the configured manager hierarchy. A majority ballot does not require every ordered approval.

optionExplanations.A: Reporting structure follows the configured manager hierarchy.
optionExplanations.B: A majority ballot does not require every ordered approval.
optionExplanations.C: A label does not build Assignments.
optionExplanations.D: One decision omits the additional required levels.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A reporting-structure approval uses Reporting Manager. The wrong manager is selected. Which relationship should be inspected first?

options.text: The current user’s operator record and configured Reporting Manager
The page’s stylesheet
A mandatory rule that every approval must wait for a deadline
An authority matrix that this approval does not use

practiceQuiz.hint: Inspect the selected model’s approver source.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Reporting Manager routing uses operator information in the current-user context. Styling does not establish reporting relationships.

optionExplanations.A: Reporting Manager routing uses operator information in the current-user context.
optionExplanations.B: Styling does not establish reporting relationships.
optionExplanations.C: A deadline is not required to identify the manager.
optionExplanations.D: The scenario explicitly uses reporting structure, not an authority matrix.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An expense requires one management level below a threshold and two above it. Which reporting-structure setting supports this?

options.text: Custom levels selected using When Rules
All levels for every expense
One level for every expense
Only a random named recipient

practiceQuiz.hint: The required depth depends on Case data.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Custom levels can select depth using conditions. All ignores the requirement for fewer levels on small expenses.

optionExplanations.A: Custom levels can select depth using conditions.
optionExplanations.B: All ignores the requirement for fewer levels on small expenses.
optionExplanations.C: One omits the second level on larger expenses.
optionExplanations.D: Random routing does not follow the specified hierarchy.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A contract needs its manager, Legal and Compliance in an ordered series. Legal and Compliance are outside the management line. Which model fits?

options.text: Authority matrix with the required ordered parties
Reporting structure that somehow reaches unrelated departments
One applicant decision
A parallel majority ballot

practiceQuiz.hint: The parties do not all belong to one hierarchy.
practiceQuiz.rationale: An authority matrix can include parties outside the reporting line. Following manager relationships does not identify unrelated departments.

optionExplanations.A: An authority matrix can include parties outside the reporting line.
optionExplanations.B: Following manager relationships does not identify unrelated departments.
optionExplanations.C: The applicant does not replace the required three parties.
optionExplanations.D: A majority ballot can omit required sign-offs.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An authority matrix is populated by a Decision table with Evaluate all rows. Several conditions match. How are approvals ordered?

options.text: The matching results populate an approver list; routing follows list order
All parties vote simultaneously and a majority wins
One party is selected randomly
The table results are ignored in favor of manager traversal

practiceQuiz.rationale: The table builds the list used for ordered approvals. This list does not establish a parallel vote.

optionExplanations.A: The table builds the list used for ordered approvals.
optionExplanations.B: This list does not establish a parallel vote.
optionExplanations.C: Random selection discards the required matching parties.
optionExplanations.D: Manager traversal describes a different model.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An approval has a configured Reject flow that resolves the Case. A director rejects it. What does this policy require?

options.text: Follow the configured rejection and resolution path
Automatically override the rejection with the VP’s vote
Automatically restart from the first manager
Count a majority across all managers

practiceQuiz.hint: Use the explicit policy rather than inventing an override.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The stated rejection configuration determines the outcome. The policy does not grant a later reviewer an automatic override.

optionExplanations.A: The stated rejection configuration determines the outcome.
optionExplanations.B: The policy does not grant a later reviewer an automatic override.
optionExplanations.D: A majority vote is not specified.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA describes cascading approval as simultaneous majority voting. What is the correction?

options.text: It represents an ordered series of approvals
It is exactly a parallel majority ballot
It cannot include human reviewers
It has no configured rejection behavior

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish a series from a ballot.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The cascade follows its ordered approvers. Parallel voting is not this model.

optionExplanations.A: The cascade follows its ordered approvers.
optionExplanations.B: Parallel voting is not this model.
optionExplanations.D: Approval and rejection flow still require configuration.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO statements distinguish the cascading models?

options.text: Reporting structure derives management levels from configured relationships
Authority matrix can include parties outside that hierarchy
Reporting structure identifies any unrelated department automatically
Authority matrix means simultaneous majority voting

practiceQuiz.hint: Compare the source of the approver list.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Management relationships define reporting-structure recipients. A populated authority matrix can name other required parties.

optionExplanations.B: A populated authority matrix can name other required parties.
optionExplanations.C: Unrelated departments are not inferred from a manager chain.
optionExplanations.D: An authority matrix supplies an ordered list, not a majority ballot.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Decision table feeding an authority matrix stops after one matching result despite several required matches. Which table setting should be checked?

options.text: Evaluate all rows
Replace the approval with one reviewer
Use an SLA to gather more table rows
Move the table into a stylesheet

practiceQuiz.hint: Inspect how matching results are collected.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Evaluate all rows collects the matching results needed for the list. One reviewer removes the multi-party requirement.

optionExplanations.A: Evaluate all rows collects the matching results needed for the list.
optionExplanations.B: One reviewer removes the multi-party requirement.
optionExplanations.C: A timer does not change table matching semantics.
optionExplanations.D: Stylesheets do not populate approval results.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A reporting-structure approval needs the entire configured hierarchy. Which setting fits?

options.text: All, using the selected Reporting Manager or Workgroup Manager source
Custom must always be used for an unconditional full chain
One automatically means the full hierarchy
A manually named list is mandatory

practiceQuiz.hint: Choose the requested number of levels.
practiceQuiz.rationale: All traverses the entire configured management hierarchy. Custom supports conditions and is unnecessary for this unconditional setting.

optionExplanations.A: All traverses the entire configured management hierarchy.
optionExplanations.B: Custom supports conditions and is unnecessary for this unconditional setting.
optionExplanations.C: One selects the immediate manager, not the whole chain.
optionExplanations.D: Reporting structure does not require a manually enumerated authority list.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the linked v7 Academy challenges, where is cascading approval configured?

options.text: Dev Studio: Approve/Reject, Cascading, then the chosen model
Only a checkbox in the Case data model
Only a runtime administration toggle
Only an adaptive prediction model

practiceQuiz.hint: Follow the documented challenge, rather than a universal Studio claim.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Both linked challenge walkthroughs use Dev Studio approval configuration. The walkthrough does not describe a data-model checkbox.

optionExplanations.A: Both linked challenge walkthroughs use Dev Studio approval configuration.
optionExplanations.B: The walkthrough does not describe a data-model checkbox.
optionExplanations.C: This is workflow design, not the stated administration toggle.
optionExplanations.D: The challenges do not configure an adaptive prediction model.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A reporting-structure approval selects Reporting Manager. The employee is the current user when the approval is reached. Where is the first manager identified?

options.text: The current employee’s operator record
An Access Group list sorted by seniority
The SLA escalation list automatically
An authority matrix required for every hierarchy

practiceQuiz.hint: Keep reporting structure distinct from authority matrix.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The selected manager relationship comes from the operator record. Access Group ordering is not the specified relationship.

optionExplanations.A: The selected manager relationship comes from the operator record.
optionExplanations.B: Access Group ordering is not the specified relationship.
optionExplanations.C: Escalation targets are not automatically the approval hierarchy.
optionExplanations.D: Authority matrix is an alternative model, not a prerequisite.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO requirements suit a cascading approval?

options.text: Several required reviewers must decide in an ordered series
The required management depth varies with Case conditions
Only simultaneous majority voting is acceptable
A single reviewer must always be replaced by several reviewers

practiceQuiz.rationale: The ordered series is the cascade’s purpose. Custom reporting levels can vary required depth.

optionExplanations.A: The ordered series is the cascade’s purpose.
optionExplanations.B: Custom reporting levels can vary required depth.
optionExplanations.C: Simultaneous majority voting calls for a different design.
optionExplanations.D: Adding reviewers without a requirement creates unnecessary work.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The current user’s reporting hierarchy is used with conditional depth. Which TWO statements are correct?

options.text: The selected manager relationship identifies the first reviewer
Conditions can choose the required number of management levels
Every reviewer is assigned simultaneously
An authority matrix is required as well

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish level count from arbitrary tier skipping.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The configured manager source identifies the first level. Conditions control depth; do not assume arbitrary middle tiers can be skipped.

optionExplanations.A: The configured manager source identifies the first level.
optionExplanations.B: Conditions control depth; do not assume arbitrary middle tiers can be skipped.
optionExplanations.C: The series is ordered rather than simultaneous.
optionExplanations.D: Reporting structure and authority matrix are alternative models.

quickRecap.value: Several required decisions in an ordered series.
Configured manager source; One, All or Custom depth.
An ordered approver list that can include other departments.
Decision table, Data Page, Activity or Data Transform.
Page List and approver property; collect matching results with Evaluate all rows.
Follow the explicitly configured rejection flow.
